mentalModelCheck.question: Why does storing 10,000,000 active user sessions in an ETS table not cause Garbage Collection pauses on worker processes?

options.label: ETS tables compress terms into gzip binaries on the worker heap before saving them.
options.explanation: ETS does not gzip terms; it stores native Erlang terms directly in off-heap C memory.

options.label: ETS memory is managed in off-heap C memory by the ERTS runtime, outside any process garbage collection heap.
options.explanation: ETS tables are allocated outside process heaps in ERTS off-heap C memory. Because individual worker heaps do not contain the ETS table data, the garbage collector never scans them during process execution.

options.label: Worker processes automatically spawn hidden threads that sweep ETS tables in the background.
options.explanation: Worker processes do not manage ETS memory; the ERTS C allocator manages table memory.

options.label: The BEAM VM disables garbage collection completely when a module calls ets:new/2.
options.explanation: Garbage collection continues running normally on process heaps for local variables.
